title: Jhalong, Bindu and the Samsing hills
start: NJP railway station or Bagdogra airport
end: NJP railway station or Bagdogra airport

cost_split.item: Reserved cars NJP–Jhalong, Jhalong–Suntalekhola, Samsing–NJP and the Bindu run, half share
Forest corporation rooms and a homestay, 4 nights with meals
Local guide for a forest-edge walk

meta_description: 4 nights in the Dooars river valleys: Jhalong and Bindu on the Jaldhaka, Suntalekhola's hanging bridge and Samsing's tea, from ₹15,000 per person.
summary: The quiet side of the Dooars, with no safari queues: two nights at Jhalong on the Jaldhaka river with a run up to Bindu at the Bhutan border, a night at the forest cottages of Suntalekhola and a night in Samsing's tea gardens. Rivers, birds and cool hill evenings for about ₹15,000 per person for two.
intro: Most Dooars trips chase rhinos. This one follows rivers. The Jaldhaka comes out of Bhutan at Bindu, where a barrage holds it back, and runs past the hydel colony at Jhalong. A few hills to the west, the Murti and its side streams leave Neora Valley National Park below Samsing. Both valleys sit at 600–900 m, cooler than the plains and full of river birds.

You stay in forest corporation rooms at Jhalong and Suntalekhola and a family homestay in Samsing. The valleys are not national parks, so they stay open in the shoulder months, though river camps close for the monsoon and roads wash out. Check current status before you travel.
highlights: Dawn on the Jaldhaka at Jhalong
Bindu barrage with Bhutan's forest across the water
Forktails and redstarts on the river boulders
Tea garden roads and Rocky Island at Samsing

days.title: NJP to Jhalong on the Jaldhaka
days.text: Leave NJP or Bagdogra by late morning, over the Coronation Bridge and through Malbazar and Chalsa, then up the Jaldhaka valley to Jhalong, about ₹4,000–5,000 for the car. Check into the forest corporation's Jholung River Camp by the water. Spend the afternoon walking along the river road and watching for plumbeous redstarts and wagtails on the stones. Bhutan's forested hills rise across the river.

days.title: Bindu and Paren
days.text: Hire a local car for a half-day, about ₹1,500–2,000. First drive up to Bindu, the last Indian village in the valley, where the barrage holds the Jaldhaka and cardamom and ginger grow on the slopes. Walk slowly through the village and look across to Bhutan; there is no crossing for travellers here. Then climb to Paren, a quiet hill village with the forest corporation's centre, for tea and the view, and return to Jhalong for lunch.

days.title: Across to Suntalekhola
days.text: After breakfast, drive down to Chalsa and up the Samsing road, through tea gardens, to Suntalekhola, about 5 km beyond Samsing. Cross the suspension footbridge to the forest corporation's cottages beside the stream that comes out of Neora Valley National Park. Spend the afternoon on the boulders with binoculars, or walk the forest edge with a local guide, about ₹500–800. Early dinner, early night; the forest is loud with insects after dark.

days.title: Rocky Island and Samsing tea
days.text: Walk back across the bridge and down the quiet 5 km road to Samsing, or take a short car ride. Check into a family homestay and go on to Rocky Island, where the Murti tumbles between huge boulders; sit, but do not swim. In the afternoon, walk the tea garden roads at about 900 m and look south over the Dooars plain as the light changes. Dinner at your homestay.

days.title: Samsing to NJP
days.text: A morning walk among the tea bushes, breakfast, then drive down through Chalsa and Malbazar and back to Siliguri, about ₹3,500–4,500 for the car. Stop for tea at Chalsa if you like. Reach NJP or Bagdogra by early afternoon; leave a buffer of two to three hours for highway traffic before an evening train or flight.

includes: Reserved cars for the main legs and the Bindu–Paren half-day, at half share
Two nights at Jholung River Camp, one at Suntaleykhola Eco-Tourism Centre and one in a Samsing homestay, with meals
One local guide for a forest-edge walk
save_money: Take the morning shared jeep from Chalsa to Jhalong instead of a reserved car from NJP, and save about ₹1,500 each.
Choose the corporation's tents at Suntalekhola, about ₹1,500, instead of a cottage.
Book a Samsing homestay directly with dinner and breakfast rather than a resort room.
good_to_know: River camps and cottages may close or flood in the monsoon; check current status before you travel.
Carry passports or ID near the Bhutan border at Bindu; there is no crossing for travellers.
Floods in October 2025 hit the Dooars rivers; check current status before you travel.
Network is weak at Jhalong, Bindu and Suntalekhola.

faqs.a: Yes, if you like rivers, birds and quiet. Jhalong is a small hydel settlement on the Jaldhaka with Bhutan's hills across the water. There is no big sight; you come for dawn on the river, the drive to Bindu and Paren, and cheap, calm nights. Two nights is right.

faqs.q: Can we cross into Bhutan at Bindu?
faqs.a: No. Bindu is a border village, but there is no crossing for travellers. Entry to Bhutan is through Phuentsholing opposite Jaigaon, with Bhutan's own documents and fees. Carry ID at Bindu and do not walk onto the barrage or across the river.

faqs.q: How do we book Jholung River Camp and Suntaleykhola?
faqs.a: Both are run by the West Bengal Forest Development Corporation and booked on wbfdc.net. Jholung has rooms at roughly ₹2,500–3,500 and Suntaleykhola cottages at about ₹2,500–3,000, with tents cheaper, all indicative. Book early for winter weekends.

River birds are the highlight: plumbeous and white-capped redstarts, forktails, wagtails, kingfishers and river lapwings on the boulders. The forest edges at Suntalekhola and Samsing add bulbuls, barbets, drongos and sometimes hornbills. Winter brings more species. Bring binoculars.

faqs.q: Is this a good honeymoon trip?
faqs.a: For couples who want quiet, yes. River cottages, cool evenings and no crowds suit a slow few days. Rooms are simple rather than romantic-resort style. If you want more comfort, book the better grade of corporation cottage or a private resort near Samsing.

faqs.q: Is there anything to do in the evenings?
faqs.a: Very little, which is the point. Dinner is early, the forest and river are loud with frogs and insects, and the sky is dark. Bring a book, a torch and warm layers for winter evenings. Some cottages have limited power backup.

Yes. Gorumara and Chapramari are about an hour from Samsing. Add a night at Murti or Lataguri and book a watchtower slot online. Remember the parks close from about mid-June to mid-September, while these river valleys stay accessible.

faqs.q: Can we do this trip by public transport?
faqs.a: Partly. Shared jeeps run from Chalsa to Jhalong and to Samsing, mostly in the morning. Suntalekhola needs a short car or the 5 km walk from Samsing. The Bindu run needs a local car. Expect waits and early starts.

faqs.q: When is the best time to go?
faqs.a: October to April, when the rivers are clear and the weather is dry. December and January nights are cold at Samsing. Spring brings more birdsong. June to September is monsoon, with high rivers, closed camps and road damage.
